Brown women’s ice hockey prepares for 2026-27 season opener at RIT
The Brown women’s ice hockey team is set to open its new season under coach Melanie Ruzzi following an improved performance last year that saw them reach the ECAC quarterfinals. Key returning players bolster both offense and defense as they prepare for their opener at RIT and welcome six newcomers.
The Brown women’s ice hockey team will begin its 2026-27 season on Friday, Oct. 16, when the Bears travel to face RIT at 6 p.m.
The Bears enter the new campaign under sixth-year head coach Melanie Ruzzi, following an 18-14-2 record in the previous season. Brown finished seventh in the ECAC standings last winter and was eliminated in the quarterfinals of the ECAC Women's Hockey Championship after a 2-1 series loss to Quinnipiac. The team advanced to that round by defeating Dartmouth 7-2 in the opening round of the tournament.
Brown’s non-conference schedule opens with two road games against RIT on Oct. 16 and 17 before moving into ECAC play on Oct. 30. Additional non-conference matchups include a road game at Providence on Nov. 28, a home contest against Assumption on Nov. 29, and a trip to Boston University on Dec. 9. After a break of over three weeks, Brown resumes with games against Sacred Heart (Jan. 1), Merrimack (Jan. 2), and Boston University (Jan. 9) to conclude its non-conference slate.
ECAC competition begins with away games at Princeton (Oct. 30) and Quinnipiac (Oct. 31). The Bears host Harvard for their first home game inside Meehan Auditorium on Nov. 6, followed by Dartmouth on Nov. 7 before embarking on a four-game road stretch through November.
Key returning players include senior Margot Norehad and junior Monique Lyons—both top goal scorers from last season with seventeen goals each; Lyons led with thirty-nine points while Norehad contributed twenty-nine points overall for Brown last year. Defensively, junior Victoria Damiani led in blocks with forty-three, supported by sophomore Isabella Gratzl and junior Ella Muralt among others.
In goal, both Rory Edwards and Anya Zupkofska return after sharing duties last season; Edwards made nineteen starts with four hundred seventy-three saves (.913 save percentage), while Zupkofska started fifteen times, recording four hundred four saves (.929 save percentage).
The program welcomes six freshmen: Keira Austen, Anika Singh, Maggie Berleth, Uma Peterson, Bogi Bahiczki-Toth, and Ryleigh Maxwell.
